incidents.summary: Spire facilitated an illegal agreement fixing initial private ophthalmology consultation fees at one hospital and agreed to settle with a £1.2 million fine.

sources.title: Private healthcare provider fixed prices with consultants - Case study - GOV.UK
sources.quote: In July 2020, the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) found that a hospital belonging to a large healthcare provider, Spire Healthcare Ltd. (a member of the Spire Healthcare Group), and 7 private, consultant eye specialists, called ophthalmologists, had entered into an illegal agreement.

sources.title: Private healthcare provider fixed prices with consultants - Case study - GOV.UK
sources.quote: It started in August 2017 and continued for at least two years until the CMA opened its investigation.

sources.title: Investegate | Company Announcement
sources.quote: Spire Healthcare apologises for its conduct and fully co-operated with the CMA in its investigation, agreeing to accept the CMA's findings in full and settle the case with a fine of £1.2m.

incidents.summary: Spire admitted failing to promptly apologise and disclose care failures to four Leeds Hospital patients and was ordered to pay a fine, surcharge and court costs.

sources.title: Spire fined for Duty of Candour failings in landmark case - LaingBuisson News
sources.quote: However, Spire did not issue letters to the four patients informing them of the concerns until November 2018, prompting the CQC to bring the prosecution – the first of its kind against an independent healthcare provider.

sources.title: Spire Healthcare pleads guilty to failing to tell four patients about poor treatment
sources.quote: Spire was fined £5000 and ordered to pay a £120 victim surcharge and £14 984.36 costs at Leeds magistrates court.

sources.title: Spire fined for Duty of Candour failings in landmark case - LaingBuisson News
sources.quote: The patients were treated by upper limb orthopaedic consultant Mike Walsh up until 2017 and suffered prolonged pain requiring further remedial surgery.

incidents.summary: A BBC Panorama investigation raised safety concerns about NHS surgery patients at Spire hospitals without intensive care facilities and medical staff contracted to work 168 hours a week.

sources.title: Spire Healthcare
sources.quote: Spire was the subject of a critical BBC Panorama investigation in April 2024, which raised safety concerns around NHS patients being treated in its hospitals.

sources.title: Spire Healthcare
sources.quote: Panorama showed an increasing number of NHS patients were undergoing surgery in Spire hospitals where no intensive care facilities were present.

sources.title: Spire Healthcare
sources.quote: Some medical staff were under contract to work 168 hours a week, over three times higher than the NHS's recommended limit.

positives: Spire Murrayfield Hospital installed over 400 solar panels on its roof and grounds.
